title: Finite product descent through rationalization and common coefficient fields
statement:
Fix the global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$, $i\in I$, be a finite pairwise disjoint open and closed cover [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

For every finite coefficient field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and put $\mathcal C_E(Y)=D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Assume the component restrictions are $\mathcal O_E$-linear equivalences $\mathcal C_E(X)\simeq\prod_i\mathcal C_E(X_i)$ and that their natural comparisons preserve completed tensor, coefficient units, and integral scalar extension for every inclusion $E\subset L$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-integral-scalar-extension].

The rationalized restrictions induce equivalences
$$D^b_c(X,E)\simeq\prod_iD^b_c(X_i,E)$$
for the raw scalar localizations of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. On Hom groups these use the canonical isomorphism
$$\left(\prod_i H_i\right)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_i\left(H_i\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\right),\qquad (h_i)_i\otimes a\longmapsto(h_i\otimes a)_i,$$
where $H_i$ are the integral component Hom modules. They commute with the coefficient extensions $E\subset L$ and preserve the rational tensor and unit of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

The common-stage restriction functor for [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] is also an equivalence
$$D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)\simeq\prod_iD^b_c(X_i,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell).$$
Every finite tuple of component objects has a preimage represented over one finite coefficient field containing their fields of definition. Every finite tuple of component morphisms has a simultaneous representative and a global preimage over one common finite extension. Two global arrows have equal component classes if and only if their representatives agree globally after some common finite extension. These comparisons respect identities, composition, tensor products and coefficient units, using the canonical finite-stage scalar-extension comparisons. At field stages $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], so these equivalences also apply to the stated finite-Tor categories. No Karoubi completion is taken. The empty product is permitted.
